question_text:
The diffusion coefficients for carbon in nickel are given at two temperatures are as follows:
\begin{tabular}{cc}
\hline$T\left({ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}\right)$ & $D\left(\mathrm{~m}^2 / \mathrm{s}\right)$ \\
\hline 600 & $5.5 \times 10^{-14}$ \\
700 & $3.9 \times 10^{-13}$ \\
\hline
\end{tabular}
(a) Determine the values of $D_0$ and $Q_d$.
(b) What is the magnitude of D at $850^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ ?

Give your answer as a tuple ($D_{0}$, $Q_{d}$, $D$ at $850^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$)The units of each required answer are (m^2/s, J/mol, m^2/s), respectively.
response:
Using the Arrhenius form \(D = D_0 \exp\!\left(-\dfrac{Q_d}{RT}\right)\) with \(T\) in kelvin:

\[
\ln\frac{D_2}{D_1} = \frac{Q_d}{R}\!\left(\frac{1}{T_1}-\frac{1}{T_2}\right)
\]

With \(T_1=873\,\text{K},\;D_1=5.5\times10^{-14}\) and \(T_2=973\,\text{K},\;D_2=3.9\times10^{-13}\):

\[
Q_d = R\,\frac{\ln(D_2/D_1)}{1/T_1-1/T_2} \approx 1.38\times10^{5}\ \text{J/mol}
\]

\[
D_0 = D_1\exp\!\left(\frac{Q_d}{RT_1}\right) \approx 1.04\times10^{-5}\ \text{m}^2/\text{s}
\]

At \(850^{\circ}\text{C}=1123\,\text{K}\):

\[
D = D_0\exp\!\left(-\frac{Q_d}{RT}\right) \approx 3.8\times10^{-12}\ \text{m}^2/\text{s}
\]

\[
\boxed{(1.04\times10^{-5},\ 1.38\times10^{5},\ 3.8\times10^{-12})}
\]
